title: Inference Unit-Economics Fabric: per-route/model/customer cost & latency attribution
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a dedicated backend microservice (the 'Unit-Economics Fabric') that computes per-request and aggregated cost and latency attribution across routes, model variants, and customers. The service will consume canonical telemetry (ingested from runtime traces and token billing events), normalize compute/cost signals (GPU time, memory, quantization profile), and produce daily/hourly breakdowns and near-real-time routing-level metrics for the Console. Goals: accurate accounting for chargeback, fine-grained SLO observability, and inputs for Optimize recommendations. This ticket covers schema design, the aggregation engine, correctness checks, and an initial rollout to internal dashboards and the chargeback pipeline. Not included: UI changes beyond dashboard wiring and billing invoicing pipeline integration (follow-ups).
implementation_notes:
- Stream sources: runtime traces (Kafka: telemetry.runtime.events) and billing tokens (Kafka: billing.events). Normalize timestamps to UTC and apply event deduplication using request_id + sequence.
- Compute model-specific multipliers using model_catalog metadata service (call with cache TTL).
- Aggregation windows: sliding 1h with 15m emit cadence for near-real-time; daily rollups for long term storage.
- Use disorder-tolerant windowing (watermarks) with 10m lateness allowance. Late events go to a correction topic and update aggregates via idempotent writes.
- Storage: columnar OLAP table in ClickHouse for fast reads; daily partitioning by date + route_id; per-customer retention policy.
- Expose read API (gRPC) for Console and Optimize; metrics endpoint for throughput/lag.
- Provide a reproducibility job that can replay raw events into the aggregation logic for audits.
- Backfill path: run replay on 90 days of raw telemetry and compare with existing chargeback numbers; generate discrepancy report automatically.
rollout_plan:
1) Dark launch: deploy Fabric to staging, consume a subset (10%) of production telemetry via sampling; validate against existing aggregates for 48h.
2) Canary: enable for internal teams and finance users only, compare daily metrics for a rolling 7-day window.
3) Gradual ramp: expand sampling to 50% and then 100% traffic for read-only use in Console (no billing changes) over 4 days.
4) Enable as canonical source for Console dashboards and Optimize recommendations after validation.
5) Switch billing/chargeback consumers after two successful billing cycles and stakeholder sign-off.
6) Post-mortem and performance tuning sprint scheduled after full rollout.
